## Claims
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has integral Schur basis indexed by partitions in \((n-r)^r\), and \(G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}\) generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- [proved] The requested graded-kernel certificate for \(G_L\) is established, using accepted task 292 for the large-\(N\) descent.

## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\), and
\[
F_L:=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z e_\rho,\qquad
\deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|.
\]
Define
\[
\pi:F_L\longrightarrow Q,\qquad e_\rho\longmapsto[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}].
\]
This is graded. It is integrally surjective: generation gives \(J_v=AG_L\), while
\(A=A_0\oplus A_+\) and \(A_0=\mathbb Z\); hence modulo \(A_+J_v\), every
\(A\)-coefficient reduces to its integral constant term.

Assume \(a\ge1\), and let \(0\ne x\in(\ker\pi)_{ij+N}\). Then
\[
x=\sum_{\substack{\rho\subseteq b^a\\|\rho|=N}}c_\rho e_\rho,
\]
and \(\pi(x)=0\) gives
\[
\sum_{|\rho|=N}c_\rho\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}
 =\sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|<N}}
 f_\lambda\bar s_{(i^j,\lambda)},\qquad
 f_\lambda\in A_{N-|\lambda|}.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, the right side initially lies in \(A_+J_v\); homogeneous expansion through
\(J_v=AG_L\) removes all indices \(|\lambda|\ge N\), since their required
coefficient degrees are respectively \(0\) (excluded by \(A_+\)) or negative.

The left side of (1) is nonzero in \(A\). For \(\rho\subseteq b^a\),
\[
(i^j,\rho)\subseteq q^r
\]
because \(b\le i\), \(a+j\le r\), and \(a+i\le q\). These partitions are distinct,
so their Schur classes are distinct members of the integral Schur basis.

For \(N>0\), the parameter tuple \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\) is valid:
\[
a+j\le r,\qquad a+i\le q,\qquad b\le i,j,\qquad 1\le N\le ab.
\]
Expand each \(f_\lambda\) in the Schur basis, producing the source-form linear
system. For every \(\beta\subseteq b^a\) with \(|\beta|=N\), its tall equation has
right side \(c_\beta\); every wide equation has right side \(0\).

Apply accepted task 292 coefficientwise. Its full-coordinate integral descent gives
\[
\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\rho_\beta)
=
\sum_{\substack{\lambda,\mu\\\mu\ne\varnothing}}
(-1)^{|\mu|+1}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}\,
\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\nu_{\lambda,\mu}),
\]
where every \(\nu_{\lambda,\mu}\) is an original wide decomposable partition.
Consequently any solution whose wide right sides vanish has every tall right side
zero. Thus \(c_\beta=0\) for every \(\beta\), contradicting \(x\ne0\).
Hence \(\ker\pi=0\) in all positive \(N\)-degrees.

For \(N=0\), \(J_v\) has no degree below \(ij\), since \(G_L\) is homogeneous of
minimum degree \(ij\). Therefore
\[
(A_+J_v)_{ij}=0.
\]
The sole degree-\(ij\) generator \(\bar s_{i^j}\) is a nonzero Schur-basis element,
so \(\pi\) is injective in degree \(ij\).

If \(a=0\), the only partition in \(b^0\) is \(\varnothing\), so \(F_L=\mathbb Z
e_\varnothing\), concentrated in degree \(ij\). The preceding \(N=0\) argument
therefore proves injectivity explicitly in this case as well.

Thus
\[
F_L\xrightarrow{\sim}Q,\qquad
Q\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}].
\]

## Gaps
None for the requested lower-adjoined graded-kernel certificate, conditional on accepted task 292.
